target.title: fix(agents): strip leaked truncation sentinels from final replies (#82121)
target.body:
## Summary
Internal truncation sentinels — `...(truncated)...`, `[... N more characters truncated]`, `...[truncated]...`, `...[additional startup memory truncated]...`, `…[truncated]` — could leak into the final user-facing assistant reply. The central sanitizer `sanitizeUserFacingText()` already strips other internal artifacts (final tags, runtime context, inbound metadata, `[tool calls omitted]`, tool-call XML) but had no rule for truncation markers, so they reached users as if they were part of the answer.

## Root Cause
- `src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers/sanitize-user-facing-text.ts` (`sanitizeUserFacingText`): the sanitizer pipeline lacked any truncation-sentinel stripping step. Producers such as `tool-result-context-guard.ts` (`[... N more characters truncated]`), the tool-transcript truncator (`...(truncated)...`), and the startup / post-compaction context truncators (`...[truncated]...`) emit these markers; when their output flows into the final reply text, the sanitizer passed it through unchanged.
- Execution path: truncation helper appends sentinel → text becomes part of the assistant final reply → `sanitizeUserFacingText()` returns it verbatim → delivered to user.

clawsweeper's review on #82121 reached the same conclusion and prescribed the fix shape: *"Add a focused final-text sanitizer rule for standalone or trailing truncation sentinel lines, with regression tests that preserve inline prose and code examples; producer-only changes would leave other sentinel sources uncovered."*

## Changes
- `src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers/sanitize-user-facing-text.ts`: add `stripTruncationSentinels()` to the sanitizer pipeline (wired at `withoutPlaceholder`, before error-context classification, so normal and error replies are both covered). It strips a fixed set of **precise** sentinel shapes (not a loose "contains truncated" match) **only when they occupy a standalone line or trail at the very end of the reply**. Sentinel-free input is returned byte-for-byte via an early `if (stripped === text) return text` short-circuit, so existing behaviour is unchanged. Matching is case-insensitive; the trailing pattern omits a leading whitespace star to avoid O(n^2) rescans on whitespace-heavy input.

## Reproduction (before fix)
The new sentinel tests fail against current `main` — the sanitizer leaks the markers:

~~~text
FAIL  strips bracketed truncation sentinels from final replies (#82121)
- Expected  ""
+ Received  "[... 5000 more characters truncated]"
FAIL  strips parenthesized truncation sentinels from final replies (#82121)
- Expected  "Partial tool output"
+ Received  "Partial tool output...(truncated)..."
~~~

## Verification (after fix)
~~~text
 ✓ src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers.sanitizeuserfacingtext.test.ts (125 tests)
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  125 passed (125)
~~~

## Test
- `pnpm test src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers.sanitizeuserfacingtext.test.ts` — 125 passed (118 pre-existing unchanged + 7 new)
- `pnpm tsgo:core` — passed
- `pnpm tsgo:core:test` — passed

New regression tests cover: stripping each sentinel family standalone + trailing; mixed ascii/unicode ellipsis (`...[truncated]…` → empty); case-insensitive variants; and **preservation** of inline code (`` `...(truncated)...` ``), code strings (`const s = "...(truncated)...";`), JSON values, code comments (`// output: [... response truncated by SDK]`), cross-line brackets, and whitespace-heavy non-matches.

## Notes
- Scope: smallest complete fix in the central sanitizer (one new helper, one wired call); producer-only changes would miss other sentinel sources (per clawsweeper).
- Safety: matching is anchored to standalone lines / end-of-reply, so prose, code, JSON, and differently-phrased brackets like `[draft truncated by user]` are preserved byte-for-byte.
- The `⚠️ [... middle content omitted ...]` marker is intentionally left untouched — the issue reports only the `truncated` families, and the omission notice is informational.

Closes #82121

target.title: fix: prevent memory flush failure from aborting user reply (#85645)
target.body:
## Summary

When `memoryFlush` fails during the reply pipeline (provider timeout, rate limit, network error), the visible error payload was treated as the final reply via `replyOperation.fail("run_failed", ...)`. This aborted the user's actual message. Since the session remained over threshold, every subsequent message triggered the same flush failure, creating a permanent death loop where no real replies could be delivered.

## Changes

**`src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.ts`**
- Memory flush visible error payloads are now logged via `logVerbose()` and **not** delivered as the reply. The main reply run proceeds normally.
- On flush exhaustion (`memoryFlushFailureCount` crosses `MAX_FLUSH_FAILURES` during the current turn), the bloated session is automatically rotated via `resetReplyRunSession()`. The old transcript file is **preserved on disk** (`cleanupTranscripts: false`) — rotation alone breaks the death loop (the new session no longer hits the bloated transcript), and keeping the old JSONL leaves it available for forensics/recovery. The active session only replays recent turns regardless of this flag.
- Added an **opt-in, non-terminal degraded notice**: when `agents.defaults.compaction.notifyUser` is enabled, flush exhaustion surfaces a short heads-up to the user via the existing `onBlockReply` bypass (same mechanism as `sendCompactionNotice`). It **never** calls `replyOperation.fail()` and **never** aborts the reply. Default (`notifyUser=false`) keeps the silent log-and-continue behavior. No new config surface is added.
- The `resetSession` / `resetSessionAfterRoleOrderingConflict` helpers are hoisted earlier in the function so they are available before the memory flush phase. No behavioral change to their existing callers; the role-ordering reset path keeps its original `cleanupTranscripts: true`.

**`src/auto-reply/reply/session.ts`**
- `initSessionState()` now clears `memoryFlushFailureCount`, `memoryFlushLastFailedAt`, and `memoryFlushLastFailureError` when a session is reset (e.g., via `/new`), preventing stale failure state from carrying over.

**`src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-session-reset.ts`**
- `resetReplyRunSession()` now clears `compactionCount` (reset to 0) and all `memoryFlush*` fields, ensuring a cleanly rotated session has no lingering flush state.

## What is NOT changed

- `runMemoryFlushIfNeeded` behavior is unchanged — it still tracks failures, increments `memoryFlushFailureCount`, and emits lifecycle events (`memory_flush_failed`, `memory_flush_exhausted`).
- `fallbacksOverride: []` is preserved — flush operations still use a fixed model/provider with no fallback chain.
- `MAX_FLUSH_FAILURES = 3` threshold is unchanged.
- No new configuration key is introduced — the opt-in notice reuses the existing `compaction.notifyUser` gate.

## Tests

- **`agent-runner-direct-runtime-config.test.ts`**: Verifies flush errors are logged and the main reply continues; verifies session rotation on flush exhaustion now uses `cleanupTranscripts: false`; covers the opt-in notice (fires on exhaustion when `notifyUser=true`, stays silent on transient failure, and never fires when `notifyUser=false`) — in all cases the main reply still proceeds.
- **`agent-runner-session-reset.test.ts`**: Verifies `compactionCount` and `memoryFlush*` fields are cleared on reset; adds a test proving that with `cleanupTranscripts: false` the session still rotates to a new id while the old transcript file is **preserved** on disk.
- **`session.test.ts`**: Verifies `initSessionState()` clears all memory flush state fields, with both in-memory assertions and persisted session store file reads.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: When `memoryFlush` / auto-compaction fails permanently (provider timeout, rate limit, 5xx), current `main` routes the visible flush error into `replyOperation.fail("run_failed")` before the main reply run, aborting the user's real reply. Because the session stays over threshold, every later message hits the same failure — a permanent death loop with no real replies delivered. This PR logs the flush failure and continues the main reply, rotates the exhausted session while preserving the old transcript on disk (`cleanupTranscripts: false`), clears stale flush state on reset, and adds an opt-in non-terminal degraded notice gated by the existing `compaction.notifyUser`.
- **Real environment tested**: OpenClaw Gateway run directly from this PR's source at current head `5dc502d76f` (branch `fix/memory-flush-death-loop-85645`) via `tsx` (`node --import tsx src/index.ts gateway run`), on macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0. Isolated state dir, `auth: none`, Gateway port `14881`. A mock OpenAI-completions provider on loopback `:3999` returns HTTP `500` for compaction/flush requests (detected by summarization-prompt keywords) and HTTP `200` for normal chat — isolating the flush-failure path while the main reply provider stays healthy. Config: `softThresholdTokens: 800`, `contextWindow: 4096`, `maxTokens: 1024`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  1. Start the mock provider: `node mock-provider/server.mjs` (loopback `:3999`, returns 500 on flush requests, 200 on normal chat).
  2. Start the Gateway from this PR's source at head `5dc502d76f`: `node --import tsx src/index.ts gateway --force --port 14881 --auth none run` with an isolated state dir.
  3. Drive 12 user messages over the WebSocket protocol: 6 to grow the session past the 800-token soft threshold, then 6 more to repeatedly trigger the (permanently failing) flush. Wait for each `agent.wait` completion.
- **Before evidence (current main)**: On current `main`, visible memory-flush error payloads are collected and passed to `replyOperation.fail("run_failed")` before the main reply run, so the user's real reply is aborted and subsequent messages repeat the failure (`src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.ts` flush-error path on `main`).
- **Evidence after fix**: Redacted runtime logs and terminal console output copied from a live OpenClaw Gateway run (`node --import tsx src/index.ts gateway --force --port 14881 --auth none run`) at head `5dc502d76f`, with private data redacted.

  Mock provider — every flush request rejected with 500 (36 flush 500s, 1 normal 200):
  ```
  [req#1]  NORMAL REQUEST — returning success
  [req#2]  FLUSH REQUEST DETECTED — returning 500
  [req#3]  FLUSH REQUEST DETECTED — returning 500
  ...
  (36 flush requests total, all returned HTTP 500)
  ```

  Gateway — flush failures logged, session mapping preserved, run continues (not aborted):
  ```
  [agent/embedded] auto-compaction failed for mock/mock-model:
    Summarization failed: 500 Mock provider: simulated flush failure
  [agent/embedded] [context-overflow-recovery] exhausted provider overflow recovery
    for mock/mock-model; livenessState=blocked suggestedAction=reset_or_new
  Auto-compaction failed (...). Preserving existing session mapping for [SESSION].
  ```

  WebSocket client — all 12 messages received a reply (`status=ok`), none aborted:
  ```
  [MSG-1]      agent done: status=ok
  [MSG-2]      agent done: status=ok
  [MSG-3]      agent done: status=ok
  [MSG-4]      agent done: status=ok
  [MSG-5]      agent done: status=ok
  [MSG-6]      agent done: status=ok
  [TRIGGER-7]  agent done: status=ok
  [TRIGGER-8]  agent done: status=ok
  [TRIGGER-9]  agent done: status=ok
  [TRIGGER-10] agent done: status=ok
  [TRIGGER-11] agent done: status=ok
  [TRIGGER-12] agent done: status=ok
  ```
- **Observed result after fix**: With the flush provider permanently broken (36 consecutive 500s), all 12 user messages still completed with `status=ok` — the death loop is gone. The flush failure is logged rather than delivered as a terminal `run_failed` reply, and the session mapping is preserved/rotated instead of aborting the turn. This is the exact condition that previously produced the permanent loop on `main`.
- **What was not tested**: Live third-party LLM providers (the flush failure is simulated with a deterministic mock 500 to make the path reproducible); long-horizon multi-session persistence across Gateway restarts; and the maintainer-judgment items (session-rotation liveness tradeoff and the opt-in notice semantics) which are product decisions rather than testable code behavior.

target.title: fix(config): return empty string for undefined in safeStringify
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: `safeStringify(undefined)` returns the literal string `"undefined"` instead of an empty value, because `JSON.stringify(undefined)` returns the value `undefined` (not a string), causing the fallthrough to `String(undefined)` → `"undefined"`.
**Solution**: Add a `value === undefined` guard in the fallback branch to return `""` instead of `String(undefined)`.
**What changed**: One line in `src/config/allowed-values.ts:29`: `return String(value)` → `return value === undefined ? "" : String(value)`.
**What did NOT change**: No API changes, no config changes, no dependency changes. Behavior for all other input types (null, number, string, object, array) is identical.

## What Problem This Solves

`safeStringify` in `src/config/allowed-values.ts` falls through to `String(value)` when `JSON.stringify` returns `undefined`. For `value === undefined`, `String(undefined)` produces the literal string `"undefined"`, which is confusing when rendered in the config form UI — a field with no value shows the text `undefined` instead of being blank. This is misleading from a user perspective — an absent value should display as empty.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: `safeStringify(undefined)` should return `""` instead of `"undefined"`.
**Real environment tested**: Direct TS function call via `node --import tsx/esm` on local workstation (Node.js v26.2.0, Linux x86_64). This mirrors the actual code path used in config UI rendering (the API response uses the same `summarizeAllowedValues` → `safeStringify` chain).

target.title: fix(tools-manager): replace spawnSync extraction with safe extractArchive API
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: `tools-manager.ts` uses `spawnSync("unzip"/"tar")` for archive extraction without any size limits, entry caps, or timeout protection, making the process vulnerable to ZIP bombs / decompression bombs if a malicious or corrupted archive is provided.

**Solution**: Replace the synchronous spawnSync-based extraction with the safe `extractArchive` API from `@openclaw/fs-safe` (re-exported from `src/infra/archive.ts`), which enforces size limits, entry count caps, timeout, and path traversal protection.

**What changed**: Removed 5 functions and 3 unused imports; added a single `extractArchiveSafe` async wrapper with explicit limits (maxArchiveBytes: 100MB, maxExtractedBytes: 500MB, maxEntries: 1000, timeoutMs: 60000). Updated tests to mock the new API.

**What did NOT change**: Extraction behavior for legitimate archives, binary discovery and installation logic, error handling for unsupported archive formats.

---

## What Problem This Solves

**Problem**: The tool manager's archive extraction had no bounds on input size or output volume, creating a denial-of-service surface through decompression bombs.

**Why This Change Was Made**: The existing `@openclaw/fs-safe` infrastructure already provides all necessary protections -- reusing it is the correct pattern rather than re-implementing limits on raw spawnSync calls.

**User Impact**: No user-visible change. Tool binaries (fd/rg) continue to download and install as before. Users and operators gain protection against oversized or malicious archives.

---

## Root Cause

**Trigger condition**: Any download of a fd or ripgrep archive from GitHub releases (or any future tool) that is corrupted or maliciously oversized.

**Root cause analysis**: `extractTarGzArchive()` and `extractZipArchive()` in `tools-manager.ts` directly shelled out to system tar/unzip without any pre-flight size check, extraction budget, or timeout. OpenClaw had a safe archive layer but the tool manager bypassed it.

**Affected scope**: All platforms (Linux, macOS, Windows). Only the tool manager (src/agents/utils/tools-manager.ts) -- other extraction paths already use `@openclaw/fs-safe`.

---

## Linked context

- **Related analysis**: Defensive programming audit Section 3.4
- **In scope**: Replacement of extraction logic in tools-manager.ts
- **Out of scope**: Other extraction sites, linting of future spawnSync extraction patterns
- **Design doc**: docs/.local/defensive-archive-extraction/design.md

---

## Real behavior proof
**Behavior addressed**: Safe archive extraction with size limits, entry caps, and timeout for tool manager downloads. The download stream byte cap now uses a Transform to reject overflow chunks *before* forwarding them to disk, and partial downloads are cleaned up on failure.

**Real environment tested**: Windows 10, Node 24, @openclaw/fs-safe@0.3.0

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
pnpm test -- src/agents/utils/tools-manager.test.ts
npx tsx _evidence_collect.mjs
```

**After-fix evidence**:
```
=== Tool Download & Extraction Evidence ===
Date: 2026-07-02T09:34:23.813Z

--- Initial state ---
Bin dir: C:\Users\Administrator\.openclaw\agent\bin
Existing fd: null
Existing rg: null

--- Download & extract fd ---
fd not found. Downloading...
fd installed to C:\Users\Administrator\.openclaw\agent\bin\fd.exe

--- Verify fd binary ---
fd --version: fd 10.4.2

--- Download & extract rg ---
ripgrep not found. Downloading...
ripgrep installed to C:\Users\Administrator\.openclaw\agent\bin\rg.exe

--- Verify rg binary ---
rg --version: ripgrep 15.1.0 (rev af60c2de9d)

=== Both fd and rg downloaded and extracted successfully ===
```

**Observed result after the fix**: Both fd and rg downloaded and extracted via `extractArchiveSafe` (wraps `@openclaw/fs-safe` with 100 MB maxArchiveBytes, 500 MB maxExtractedBytes, 1000 maxEntries, 60s timeout). Both binaries verified as executable. Unit tests pass (7/7). The Transform-based stream limiter rejects overflow chunks *before* forwarding them, and partial downloads are cleaned up. This closes both the proof gap and the stream-cap defect identified in review.

**What was not tested**: Extraction from a deliberately oversized/malicious archive (the stream cap and archive limits are unit-tested; extraction limits are independently verified in @openclaw/fs-safe tests).
## Tests and validation

### Unit tests

```
 RUN  v4.1.8

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  5 passed (5)
```

### Integration / E2E

The @openclaw/fs-safe package's extractArchive is independently tested in src/infra/archive.test.ts for: archive size limits, entry count limits, symlink/hardlink traversal protection, absolute entry path rejection, staged extraction with safe merge.

## Risk checklist

- [x] This change is backwards compatible
- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations
- [ ] I have updated relevant documentation (N/A -- no docs reference the old extraction functions)
- [ ] Breaking changes (if any) are documented in Summary
- Merge-risk explanation: Low risk. The extractArchive API is already used by src/infra/install-flow.ts and extensions/signal/src/install-signal-cli.ts in production. The replacement is mechanical -- same archive formats, same extraction semantics, with additional safety bounds.

---

## 🔧 Post-review fix (2026-07-02)

**Problem**: The PR HEAD (9077b05282) replaced `src/agents/utils/tools-manager.ts` with a one-line placeholder, removing `ensureTool`/`getToolPath` exports.

**Fix**: Restored the full implementation via the correct Transform-stream-limit commit. The branch now contains:
- Full tools-manager.ts implementation with all exports restored
- Transform stream cap that rejects overflow chunks *before* they reach disk
- Completion-guarded pipeline with partial download cleanup
- Safe `extractArchive` API from `@openclaw/fs-safe` with size limits

**Verification**: ✅ 7/7 unit tests passed | ✅ Type check clean | ✅ Both exports (ensureTool, getToolPath) confirmed

target.title: fix(codex): keep mirrored tool results out of inline transcript updates
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An internal Codex app-server tool result can be mirrored into an OpenClaw session transcript as a `toolResult` message. That transcript record is useful for context, debugging, and replay, but the mirror path also published the same `toolResult` as an inline transcript-update `message`.

Downstream live-update and delivery consumers treat inline transcript-update messages as immediately displayable. If the tool result is a failed command output, a raw traceback or command failure can leak into the source chat even though the assistant's terminal reply was silent or otherwise unrelated.

## Why This Change Was Made

`mirrorCodexAppServerTranscript()` already appends only user, assistant, and tool-result messages into the session JSONL. The bug was not persistence; the bug was publishing all appended mirror messages as inline update payloads:

- `user` and `assistant` are safe inline update messages.
- `toolResult` is an internal context artifact and should remain persisted, but should not be sent as an inline display/delivery update.

This PR keeps `toolResult` records in the transcript while publishing their update as sequence-only metadata. Consumers that need a fresh transcript can still refresh by `messageSeq`, but display/delivery paths do not receive raw tool output as `update.message`.

## User Impact

This prevents failed internal tool output such as Python tracebacks, shell stderr, or JSON parser errors from appearing as visible chat messages when the Codex app-server transcript mirror publishes a turn update.

The assistant-visible transcript remains intact for replay/debugging, so this should not reduce model continuity or operator forensic value.

## Implementation

- Adds a small publication boundary in `extensions/codex/src/app-server/transcript-mirror.ts`.
- Publishes inline `message` only for mirrored `user` and `assistant` records.
- Still publishes `messageId` and `messageSeq` for `toolResult` records so sequence tracking and refresh behavior remain stable.
- Adds focused regressions in `transcript-mirror.test.ts`:
  - a failed `toolResult` with `JSONDecodeError` is persisted but not emitted inline;
  - a mixed user/tool-result/assistant batch keeps stable sequence numbers while hiding the tool-result body from live updates.

## Evidence

### Focused regression

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-codex-app-server-support.config.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/transcript-mirror.test.ts
```

Result:

```text
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  16 passed (16)
```

### Type check

```sh
pnpm tsgo:extensions
```

Result: passed.

### Formatting and whitespace

```sh
git diff --check
pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 extensions/codex/src/app-server/transcript-mirror.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/transcript-mirror.test.ts
```

Result: both passed.

### Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: actual transcript mirror publication, without mocking `publishSessionTranscriptUpdateByIdentity`.

Command run after this patch:

```sh
node --import tsx --input-type=module <<'NODE'
import fs from 'node:fs/promises';
import os from 'node:os';
import path from 'node:path';
import { onInternalSessionTranscriptUpdate } from './src/sessions/transcript-events.ts';
import { attachCodexMirrorIdentity, mirrorCodexAppServerTranscript } from './extensions/codex/src/app-server/transcript-mirror.ts';

const dir = await fs.mkdtemp(path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'openclaw-mirror-proof-'));
const sessionFile = path.join(dir, 'session.jsonl');
const updates = [];
const unsubscribe = onInternalSessionTranscriptUpdate((update) => updates.push(update));
try {
  await mirrorCodexAppServerTranscript({
    sessionFile,
    sessionId: 'session-proof',
    sessionKey: 'agent:proof:main',
    messages: [
      attachCodexMirrorIdentity({
        role: 'toolResult',
        toolCallId: 'call-json',
        toolName: 'bash',
        isError: true,
        content: [{
          type: 'toolResult',
          toolCallId: 'call-json',
          toolName: 'bash',
          content: 'Traceback\njson.decoder.JSONDecodeError: Unterminated string',
        }],
        timestamp: Date.now(),
      }, 'turn-proof:tool:call-json:result'),
    ],
    idempotencyScope: 'codex-app-server:thread-proof',
  });
} finally {
  unsubscribe();
}
const raw = await fs.readFile(sessionFile, 'utf8');
console.log(JSON.stringify({
  persistedToolResult: raw.includes('"role":"toolResult"') && raw.includes('JSONDecodeError'),
  emittedUpdates: updates.length,
  updateHasInlineMessage: updates.some((update) => update.message !== undefined),
  updateLeaksTracebackText: JSON.stringify(updates).includes('JSONDecodeError'),
  updateMessageSeqs: updates.map((update) => update.messageSeq),
}, null, 2));
await fs.rm(dir, { recursive: true, force: true });
NODE
```

Observed result after fix:

```json
{
  "persistedToolResult": true,
  "emittedUpdates": 1,
  "updateHasInlineMessage": false,
  "updateLeaksTracebackText": false,
  "updateMessageSeqs": [
    1
  ]
}
```

## Risk

Low-to-medium. This changes only the live publication shape for Codex app-server mirrored `toolResult` records, not transcript persistence.

Expected behavior changes:

- live inline consumers no longer receive `toolResult` bodies from this mirror path;
- consumers still receive sequence metadata and can refresh transcript state if they need the full raw transcript.

What was not tested:

- a full end-to-end Matrix source-chat run against a live gateway instance;
- browser/UI rendering of transcript history after a sequence-only `toolResult` update.

## Non-Goals

- This does not stop persisting tool results in session JSONL.
- This does not alter user or assistant mirror dedupe behavior.
- This does not change explicit message-tool delivery.

target.title: fix(cron): skip deleteAfterRun and preserve counters for manual runs (#83538)
target.body:
## Summary

`openclaw cron run` (manual/debug runs) on a `deleteAfterRun` at-job deletes the job on success — consuming the one-shot and preventing its scheduled execution. Manual runs also mutate `consecutiveErrors`/`consecutiveSkipped` counters, interfering with scheduled retry/backoff state.

This PR adds an `isManual` flag to `applyJobResult` so manual runs preserve the job and leave scheduled execution state untouched.

## Root cause

`applyJobResult()` has no concept of manual vs scheduled runs. When a manual run succeeds on a `deleteAfterRun: true` at-job, `shouldDelete` evaluates to `true` and the job is removed from the store — the scheduled fire never happens.

Additionally, manual error/skipped/success outcomes unconditionally mutate `consecutiveErrors` and `consecutiveSkipped` counters, which control retry backoff and auto-disable behavior for scheduled runs.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `timer.ts` | Add `isManual` option to `applyJobResult`; skip `deleteAfterRun` for manual runs; guard all counter mutations and alert emissions with `!isManual` |
| `ops.ts` | Pass `isManual: true` from manual run completion and invalid-persisted-run handling |
| `timer.regression.test.ts` | 5 new tests: manual ok/error preserve job, manual doesn't increment/reset counters |

## Tests

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts
 ✓ cron (45 tests) 144ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  45 passed (45)
```

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Manual `cron run` on a `deleteAfterRun` at-job deletes it, preventing scheduled execution. Manual runs also mutate scheduled retry counters.

### Manual-run state contract

`cron run` is a debug/verification command. Manual runs record their outcome (lastRunAtMs, lastStatus, lastError) but do not advance scheduled state. This makes manual runs safe, non-destructive operations that cannot interfere with scheduled execution. No reasonable user scenario depends on manual runs consuming one-shot jobs or driving retry/backoff state.

## Real behavior proof (Docker, HEAD `8596607fca`, 2026-06-02 — backoff fix)

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Manual `cron run` on a recurring job that errors must not open a backoff window that blocks the next scheduled fire. Previously, `isErrorBackoffPending()`, `resolveJobErrorBackoffUntilMs()`, `isPendingErrorBackoffSlot()`, and `recomputeJobNextRunAtMs()` read `lastRunStatus` and `lastRunAtMs` without checking `lastRunWasManual`, causing a manual error to push `nextRunAtMs` forward and block the timer-scheduled fire.

- **Real environment tested**: Docker container `node:24-bookworm` (linux/arm64), Node.js `v24.16.0`, Vitest `v4.1.7`, patched OpenClaw at commit `8596607fca`.

A recurring every-job with `lastRunWasManual: true` and `lastRunStatus: "error"` would have `resolveJobErrorBackoffUntilMs()` return a backoff deadline, `isErrorBackoffPending()` would return `true`, and `isRunnableJob()` would return `false` — blocking the next scheduled fire. `recomputeJobNextRunAtMs()` would also push `nextRunAtMs` forward to the backoff floor. Test file authored as part of this PR.

target.body:
## Summary
- Preserve Discord reply text when a media attachment is rejected with HTTP 413 by retrying the same reply as text-only.
- Carry the fallback send result on the thrown delivery error so durable delivery can record the partial send instead of losing the message evidence.
- Merge adapter-reported partial results in outbound delivery, including best-effort sends that continue after the failed payload.

## Change Type
- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security
- [ ] Chore

## Scope
- [ ] Gateway
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] Auth
- [ ] Memory
- [x] Integrations
- [ ] API
- [ ] UI/UX
- [ ] CI

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** A Discord reply with text plus an oversized media attachment now sends the text fallback and exposes that sent message as partial delivery evidence when the media upload fails with HTTP 413.

**Environment tested:** Local Linux checkout on branch `fix/99021-discord-oversize-attachment`, Node via `node --import tsx`, targeted Vitest suites through `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs`.

**Steps run after the patch:** Called the actual Discord outbound adapter and outbound delivery core from source with `node --import tsx --no-warnings -e`, then ran the targeted Discord, outbound delivery, and durable message tests.

**Evidence after fix:**

**Observed result:** The production adapter first attempted the media reply, then retried the same text without media after the 413; the thrown error carried `sentBeforeError: true` plus the fallback Discord message result. The outbound delivery core also preserved adapter partial results when best-effort delivery continued to the next payload.

**Not tested:** A live Discord guild upload with real credentials and an actual over-limit attachment was not run; the proof exercises the production adapter and delivery functions with injected send dependencies to avoid external network side effects.

## Root Cause
- Discord rejected oversized media attachments before the reply text could be delivered, and the adapter did not retry the text-only portion.
- The outbound core already tracked prior successful payloads, but it did not read adapter-reported partial results from thrown errors in every path.

## Regression Test Plan
- `extensions/discord/src/outbound-adapter.test.ts` covers 413 media rejection, text-only fallback, and avoiding duplicate fallback when a lower Discord path already reports send evidence.
- `src/infra/outbound/deliver.test.ts` covers merging partial adapter results with earlier payloads and preserving those results in best-effort continuation.
- `src/channels/message/send.test.ts` verifies the durable message layer still maps partial outbound errors to `partial_failed` receipts.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes
When Discord rejects an oversized attachment, users still receive the reply text instead of losing the entire response. Delivery accounting records the text fallback as partial delivery evidence so retry/recovery paths do not treat it as a total no-send.

## Security Impact
- New permissions? No
- Secrets handling changed? No
- New network calls? No

target.title: fix(tts): defer text settlement for final-mode TTS to eliminate churn (#83511)
target.body:
## Summary

When `messages.tts.mode = "final"`, the Telegram bot exhibited text "churn" — users would briefly see a text message appear, then it would be deleted and replaced by a voice note with the same text as caption. This happened on **both** the ACP dispatch path and the non-ACP dispatch path (`dispatch-from-config.ts`).

This PR eliminates the churn on **both paths** by introducing a `captionedFinalText` channel capability, suppressing live block delivery and partial streaming when captioned final TTS will be used, and correctly handling tagged auto-TTS mode with a split eligibility boolean.

## Root cause

```
Before (main):
  1. Block text / partial streaming delivers text to user immediately
  2. TTS synthesis runs (2-5 seconds)
  3. Voice note + caption delivered as separate message
  Result: user sees text first, then voice note = churn (#83511)

After (this PR):
  1. willUseCaptionedFinalTts = true (channel supports captioned voice + final TTS mode)
  2. Partial streaming suppressed, block text delivery suppressed
  3. TTS synthesis runs, text accumulated silently
  4. Voice note + caption delivered as single message (or text fallback if TTS fails)
  Result: user sees only the voice note with caption = no churn
```

### Tagged auto-TTS mode

When `messages.tts.auto: "tagged"`, TTS only fires for replies containing `[[tts:...]]` directives. Three additional issues were discovered and fixed:

1. **Split boolean**: `willUseCaptionedFinalTts` was doing two jobs — gating live text suppression AND caption eligibility. Split into `willUseCaptionedFinalTts` (live text suppression, excludes tagged) and `canCaptionFinalTts` (caption eligibility, includes tagged).

2. **Block TTS gate**: The accumulated block TTS fallback was gated on `replies.length === 0`, but Anthropic streaming returns both block callbacks and a final reply payload. Changed to gate on `deliveredFinalTtsMedia` and `queuedFinal` instead.

3. **Partial streaming leak**: `onPartialReply` was active for tagged mode, sending raw `[[tts:text]]...[[/tts:text]]` directive text to Telegram during streaming, creating a duplicate text message before the voice+caption arrived. Fixed by gating `onPartialReply` with `canCaptionFinalTts` (covers both always and tagged modes) instead of `willUseCaptionedFinalTts`.

### Media block preservation

When captioned final TTS is active, block suppression is narrowed to **text-only** payloads. Blocks containing media (`mediaUrl`, `mediaUrls`), `presentation`, `interactive`, or `channelData` are delivered immediately with their text stripped (to avoid duplicating the caption). This applies to both ACP and non-ACP dispatch paths.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.ts` | `willUseCaptionedFinalTts` + `canCaptionFinalTts`: suppress partial streaming and block text for both always and tagged modes; narrow block suppression to text-only payloads (media blocks delivered with text stripped); `sendFinalPayload` returns `deliveredMedia`; block TTS gate changed from `replies.length === 0` to `!deliveredFinalTtsMedia && !queuedFinal` |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.test.ts` | Regression tests: tagged directive-only voice+caption, tagged+always both-block-and-final delivery, partial suppression for tagged TTS on caption-capable channels, plain tagged block delivery, media block delivery with text stripped, text-only block suppression |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.ts` | `willUseCaptionedFinalTts` gate: suppress ACP block delivery and defer text settlement; `canCaptionFinalTts` for tagged mode; `deliveredFinalTtsMedia` tracking |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp-delivery.ts` | `deliveredFinalTtsMedia` state tracking + `hasDeliveredFinalTtsMedia()` accessor; narrow `suppressBlockUserDelivery` to text-only blocks (media blocks delivered with text stripped) |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp-delivery.test.ts` | Regression tests: media block delivery with text stripped under `suppressBlockUserDelivery`, text-only block suppression |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.test.ts` | Regression tests: deferred settlement, block suppression, tagged streaming, tagged directive TTS, ACP live text deferral |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/acp-projector.ts` | `deferLiveTextUntilFinalFlush` option to suppress live text flushing for tagged TTS |
| `src/tts/directives.ts` | `resolveDirectiveOnlyTtsCaptionText` parser helper to extract clean caption from directive-only responses |
| `extensions/telegram/src/shared.ts` | `captionedFinalText: true` capability declaration |
| `extensions/telegram/src/shared.test.ts` | Test for capability declaration |
| `src/channels/plugins/types.core.ts` | JSDoc for `captionedFinalText` capability contract |
| `src/channels/plugins/tts-capabilities.test.ts` | Capability seam test |
| `docs/tools/tts.md` | Document `captionedFinalText` capability: opt-in criteria via `capabilities.tts.voice`, tagged mode behavior, text-only fallback, plugin API snippet |
| `docs/plugins/sdk-channel-plugins.md` | Document `captionedFinalText` capability in channel plugin SDK guide: opt-in declaration, media block preservation, fallback behavior, tagged mode |
| `docs/.generated/plugin-sdk-api-baseline.sha256` | Updated SDK API baseline hash |

## Tests

```
$ npx vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.test.ts
 ✓ 202 passed (202)

$ npx vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp-delivery.test.ts
 ✓ 29 passed (29)

$ npx vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.test.ts
 ✓ 50 passed (50)

$ npx vitest run extensions/telegram/src/shared.test.ts
 ✓ 11 passed (11)

$ npx vitest run src/channels/plugins/tts-capabilities.test.ts
 ✓ 1 passed (1)

Total: 293 tests passed across 5 test suites
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Telegram TTS final-mode text-before-voice churn on both ACP and non-ACP dispatch paths, plus tagged mode partial preview leaking raw `[[tts:text]]` directives, plus media block suppression during captioned final TTS.

- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout at commit `05b4483a8f`, macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0. Live Telegram bot (`@thomas_fu_bot`) with Microsoft TTS (`zh-CN-XiaoxiaoNeural`), `messages.tts.mode: "final"`.

- **Failing proof before fix (live Telegram)**:

  ![Before fix — separate text message + voice message (churn)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jerry-Xin/openclaw/proof-images-83988/.proof-images/83988-before-fix.png)

  User sent "hello" to the Telegram bot. The bot responded with **two separate messages**: a text message AND a voice note — instead of a single voice note with caption.

- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  1. Built and installed from current head: `npm run build && npm pack && npm install -g openclaw-2026.6.2.tgz`
  2. Registered and restarted Gateway: `openclaw gateway install && openclaw gateway restart`
  3. Tested with `messages.tts.auto: "always"` and `messages.tts.auto: "tagged"` — sent plain messages and directive-bearing messages to `@thomas_fu_bot` on Telegram

- **Evidence after fix**: Always mode (`messages.tts.auto: "always"`) at commit `05b4483a8f`:

  ![Always mode — voice with caption, single message](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jerry-Xin/openclaw/proof-images-83988/.proof-images/83988-always-mode.png)

  Always-mode replies produce a single voice note with caption text. No text churn, no separate text bubble.

- **Evidence — Media block preservation with captioned final TTS at commit `05b4483a8f`**:

  ![Media block preserved — image delivered + voice note with caption](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jerry-Xin/openclaw/proof-images-83988/.proof-images/83988-media-block.png)

  When the bot generates an image during a TTS-enabled conversation (`auto: "always"`), the image is delivered immediately while text is deferred to the voice note caption. No media blocks are suppressed, and caption text does not duplicate as a separate text message.

- **Observed result after fix**: Always TTS auto mode delivers voice notes as single messages with caption text on Telegram. Media blocks (images, files) are preserved and delivered immediately with text stripped. No text flash, no duplicate messages, no media loss.

- **What was not tested**: Other TTS providers (only Microsoft TTS tested live). Group chat TTS (tested in DM only). Other channels with `captionedFinalText` capability (only Telegram tested). Tagged mode live proof pending — covered by unit tests (partial suppression + directive-only caption regression tests added).

Closes #83511

target.title: fix(matrix): reverse-proxy path support for Matrix homeserver URLs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Matrix channel connections fail for homeservers deployed behind reverse proxies with path prefixes (e.g., `https://host/proxy/base/`). The previous implementation incorrectly constructed transport URLs by using absolute paths, causing `new URL()` to strip the reverse-proxy path prefix and resolve only against the origin.

Users deploying Matrix homeservers in containerized environments, FaaS platforms, or any setup requiring a reverse-proxy path prefix would experience connection failures even with valid credentials and network access.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix moves URL construction entirely to the transport layer by ensuring endpoints are resolved relative to the full homeserver base path. The `apiPrefix` config surface was removed following ClawSweeper review as it was not carried through the runtime (`resolveMatrixConfigForAccount`, `MatrixAuth`, client keying, or `createMatrixClient`), making it a no-op for normal paths.

Key changes:
- `transport.ts`: `normalizeEndpoint()` strips leading slashes so `new URL(endpoint, baseUrl)` resolves relative to the full base path; `performMatrixRequest()` ensures the homeserver URL ends with `/` so it's treated as a directory
- `http-client.ts`: Replaced public `apiPrefix` parameter with private `DEFAULT_API_PREFIX` constant for bare-path resolution only
- Removed unused `apiPrefix` from `MatrixClient` constructor, config schema, and types

This approach keeps the fix minimal and transport-local without introducing new config surfaces that would require migration, validation, and lifecycle management.

## Linked context

- Fixes reverse-proxy path prefix resolution for Matrix channel connections
- No related open issues found
- No known affected releases (config was never shipped)

## User Impact

Matrix channel users running homeservers behind reverse proxies with path prefixes (e.g., `https://host/proxy/base/`) can now successfully connect and communicate. Previously, these deployments would fail during transport URL construction because the leading slash in endpoint paths caused `new URL()` to resolve against the origin only, stripping the proxy path.

No action required from existing users—this is a transparent fix. No new config options were added; instead, an unused `apiPrefix` config surface was removed as part of narrowing the scope.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- **Behavior addressed**: Matrix channel fails to connect when the homeserver URL includes a reverse-proxy path prefix (e.g., https://host/proxy/base/).
- **Real environment tested**: Linux x64, Node 24.13.1, target homeserver (Conduit fork) behind openresty reverse proxy with path prefix at `https://faas-msp.uat.zte.com.cn/faas-function/paas-uat/tuwunel-openclaw-test/`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**: 
```
openclaw config set channels.matrix.homeserver "https://faas-msp.uat.zte.com.cn/faas-function/paas-uat/tuwunel-openclaw-test/"
openclaw gateway run --bind loopback --port 18789 --force
openclaw channels status --probe
```
- **Evidence after fix**:
  ![Matrix Channel Status](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7802eb0e-418e-4b58-8022-ee5a2126dd8b)
  ![Matrix Channel Configuration](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/058e949b-862c-4bde-a618-cdf2618e4f60)
- **Observed result after fix**: 
  - `channels status --probe` outputs: `Matrix default: enabled, configured, running, connected, transport:just now, health:healthy, url:https://faas-msp.uat.zte.com.cn/faas-function/paas-uat/tuwunel-openclaw-test/, works`
  - Gateway logs show Matrix plugin successfully connected to the path-prefixed homeserver and joined rooms
  - No URL construction errors in gateway logs
- **Not tested**: Live message send/receive round-trip through the path-prefixed homeserver (relies on homeserver-side routing which is out of scope for this transport-layer fix).

## Tests and validation

- **1393 tests passed** (121 test files) in `extensions/matrix/`
- **New focused test coverage** (2026-07-02): 4 transport tests for path-prefixed URL resolution:
  1. `resolves path-prefixed homeserver endpoint correctly` — verifies `https://host/proxy/base/` + `/_matrix/...` → `https://host/proxy/base/_matrix/...`
  2. `resolves standard homeserver endpoint correctly` — backward compat: `https://matrix.example.org/` unchanged
  3. `handles homeserver URL without trailing slash` — `https://host/proxy/base` still resolves correctly (trailing slash added)
  4. `passes through absolute endpoint when allowed` — absolute URLs are forwarded as-is
- Standard homeserver URLs (`https://matrix.example.org`) continue to work correctly
- No regressions in existing Matrix channel functionality

## AI-Assisted PR Checklist

- [x] AI-assisted (generated with AI coding agent)
- [x] Human-run real behavior proof included above with screenshots and live `channels status --probe` output
- [x] I understand what the code does: `normalizeEndpoint()` strips leading `/` so `new URL()` resolves URLs relative to the full homeserver base path instead of just the origin
- [x] Resolved bot review conversations after addressing them (added real behavior proof, removed unused config surface per ClawSweeper review, added focused transport tests)

## Risk checklist

**Compatibility**: 
- ✅ Config `apiPrefix` was never shipped to any release — no existing users affected
- ✅ Standard homeserver URLs unaffected — backward compatible URL resolution
- ✅ Migration not needed — config surface removed before any release
- ✅ Focused regression tests added covering both path-prefixed and standard URL resolution

**Message delivery**:  
- ✅ Transport-only change — only affects HTTP URL construction, not message formatting or delivery contracts
- ✅ Channel contract unchanged — send/receive/status methods identical signatures
- ✅ Proven pattern — follows same URL resolution pattern used by Discord, Slack, Telegram channel plugins

**Security**:
- ✅ SSRF protections remain fully in place
- ✅ No new config surfaces that could be misconfigured

## Current review state

- Codex review requested real behavior proof and regression coverage — addressed above with 4 new transport tests, screenshots, and live `channels status --probe` output
- All known concerns addressed: proof, compatibility, message delivery safety, regression coverage

target.title: fix(security): use constant-time comparison for TLS fingerprint verification
target.body:
## Summary

TLS certificate fingerprint verification in `src/gateway/client.ts` uses `!==` (standard JavaScript string equality), which is vulnerable to **timing side-channel attacks** (CWE-208).

An attacker on the network path can measure response time differences to iteratively guess the correct fingerprint byte-by-byte, potentially bypassing TLS pinning for MITM attacks on gateway connections.

## Root cause

Two locations perform fingerprint comparison with `!==`:

| Location | Context |
|----------|---------|
| Line 205 | WebSocket `checkServerIdentity` callback |
| Line 681 | HTTP `validateTlsFingerprint` method |

## Fix

Replace both with `safeEqualSecret()` from `src/security/secret-equal.ts`, which uses `SHA-256` hashing + `crypto.timingSafeEqual` for constant-time comparison.

This is the **same function already used** for pairing token verification elsewhere in the codebase — just missed for TLS fingerprints.

```diff
- if (fingerprint !== expected) {
+ if (!safeEqualSecret(fingerprint, expected)) {
```

## Why safeEqualSecret and not raw timingSafeEqual

`timingSafeEqual` requires both buffers to have equal length, which would leak the length of the expected fingerprint. `safeEqualSecret` avoids this by hashing both values with SHA-256 first (producing fixed 32-byte digests), then comparing the digests in constant time.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm tsgo` — compiles cleanly
- [x] `pnpm check` — lint/format passes
- [x] Existing `safeEqualSecret` tests in `src/security/audit-extra.sync.test.ts` cover equal, unequal, different-length, and undefined inputs
- [x] No remaining `fingerprint !== expected` patterns in codebase

target.title: fix(agents): add additionalProperties:false to Anthropic tool inputSchema for Opus 4.8 compat
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`tools.profile=coding` + `anthropic/claude-opus-4-8` returns HTTP 400 because opus-4-8 enforces **JSON Schema draft 2020-12** validation on tool `input_schema` (opus-4-7 was lenient). When tool parameters contain draft-07 tuple syntax, the Anthropic API rejects the request.

**Root cause**: `additionalProperties: false` is not the real issue — opus-4-8 accepts schemas without `additionalProperties` (200 OK). The real cause is that draft-07 tuple `items: [...]` and `additionalItems` syntax was replaced by `prefixItems` in draft 2020-12. opus-4-8 rejects schemas containing these legacy constructs with:

```
400 tools.0.custom.input_schema: JSON schema is invalid.
It must match JSON Schema draft 2020-12
```

**Fix**: Add `normalizeAnthropicSchema`, a recursive normalizer that converts all draft-07 tuple syntax to draft 2020-12 at the Anthropic-specific choke point (`projectAnthropicTools`), while preserving the existing `additionalProperties: false`.

## Conversion Rules (pure syntax rename, zero semantic change)

| draft-07 | draft 2020-12 |
|----------|---------------|
| `items: [A, B, C]` | `prefixItems: [A, B, C]` (delete `items`) |
| `additionalItems: X` | `items: X` (delete `additionalItems`) |
| `items: {...}` (single schema) | unchanged |
| `items: false` | unchanged |

Identity-preserving: returns the original object reference when no changes are needed. Recursively traverses all JSON Schema nesting keywords: `properties`, `$defs`, `definitions`, `dependentSchemas`, `patternProperties`, `anyOf`, `oneOf`, `allOf`, `if`/`then`/`else`, `not`, `contains`, `items`, `prefixItems`, `additionalProperties`, `propertyNames`.

## Architecture

The fix applies at the **single Anthropic-specific choke point** (`projectAnthropicTools`), keeping the shared `projectRuntimeToolInputSchema()` provider-agnostic:

```
All upstream schema sources (Zod / TypeBox / MCP / Plugin SDK / user-defined)
         ↓
  projectRuntimeToolInputSchema()  ← shared: JSON-ifies schema, checks violations (no provider logic)
         ↓
  projectAnthropicTools()          ← Anthropic-specific choke point
    └─ normalizeAnthropicSchema()  ← NEW: recursive draft 2020-12 normalization (Anthropic only)
         ↓
  input_schema                     ← sent to Anthropic API
```

Both Anthropic API consumers share the same path:
- [anthropic-transport-stream.ts:562](src/agents/anthropic-transport-stream.ts#L562) — agent transport
- [anthropic.ts:1489](src/llm/providers/anthropic.ts#L1489) — provider path

Reference implementation: `normalizeOpenAIStrictCompatSchemaRecursive` ([provider-tools.ts:216](src/plugin-sdk/provider-tools.ts#L216)) — same recursive traversal pattern.

## Files Changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/agents/anthropic-schema-normalizer.ts` | **New** — recursive draft 2020-12 normalizer (104 lines) |
| `src/agents/anthropic-schema-normalizer.test.ts` | **New** — 18 test cases |
| `src/agents/anthropic-tool-projection.ts` | **Modified** — `additionalProperties: false` + `normalizeAnthropicSchema()` call at the Anthropic-specific choke point |
| `src/agents/anthropic-transport-stream.test.ts` | **Modified** — regression assertion for `additionalProperties: false` |
| `src/llm/providers/anthropic.test.ts` | **Modified** — regression assertion for `additionalProperties: false` |

## Evidence

### Tests: 158/158 passing

```
$ pnpm test src/agents/anthropic-schema-normalizer.test.ts \
  src/agents/tool-schema-projection.test.ts \
  src/agents/anthropic-transport-stream.test.ts \
  src/agents/anthropic-payload-policy.test.ts \
  src/llm/providers/anthropic.test.ts

 Test Files  5 passed (5)
      Tests  158 passed (158)
```

### Lint / Format / Typecheck

| Check | Result |
|-------|--------|
| oxlint | zero errors, zero warnings |
| oxfmt | correct formatting |

### New test coverage matrix

| Scenario | Assertion |
|----------|-----------|
| No-change identity-preserving | `expect(normalize(s)).toBe(s)` |
| `items: [A, B]` → `prefixItems` | `{ type: "array", prefixItems: [...] }` |
| `items: {...}` single schema unchanged | `toBe(s)` |
| `items: false` unchanged | `toBe(s)` |
| Existing `prefixItems` not overwritten | preserves existing `prefixItems` |
| Empty `items: []` → empty `prefixItems` | `{ prefixItems: [] }` |
| `additionalItems: false` → `items: false` | `{ items: false }` |
| `additionalItems: {...}` → `items: {...}` | schema correctly transferred |
| Does not overwrite existing `items` | preserves existing `items` |
| `items` tuple + `additionalItems` together | `prefixItems` + `items` |
| Deep nesting in `properties` | recursive conversion |
| Tuple inside `anyOf` | recursive conversion |
| `oneOf` + `allOf` combination | recursive conversion |
| Tuple inside `$defs` | recursive conversion |
| `additionalItems` in `properties` values | recursive conversion |
| Multi-level deep nesting | through anyOf→properties→array |

### Live API verification (credit: @brandencho)

Verified against real opus-4-8 API with single-tool requests:

| tool input_schema | result |
|-------------------|--------|
| no top-level `additionalProperties` | ✅ 200 |
| `+ additionalProperties: false` | ✅ 200 |
| `patternProperties`, `anyOf+null`, `{}`, `additionalProperties:true`, dangling `$ref` | ✅ 200 |
| tuple `items: [...]` (draft-07) | ❌ 400 "must match JSON Schema draft 2020-12" |
| tuple `items: [...]` + `additionalProperties: false` (previous PR) | ❌ 400 |
| `prefixItems: [...]` (draft 2020-12) | ✅ 200 |

target.title: feat(durable): add durable session task runtime foundation
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

This PR adds the opt-in, local-first durable runtime foundation proposed by PR1. The target failure mode is coordinator silence: long-running session/task/subagent work can continue across many steps, branches, and process restarts, but operators and runtime code need a bounded durable projection of which run, step, child, signal, or recovery state is open.

This is not a general-purpose workflow engine and does not include Work module, Workboard UI/tools, Task Flow projection adapters, or product-specific logic.

## Dependency Chain

This is PR2 in the replacement durable runtime stack:

1. PR1: durable session/task runtime RFC v2.
2. PR2: durable runtime foundation, this PR.
3. PR3: agent/session/subagent wiring on top of this foundation.

This PR is designed to be reviewable independently as a core foundation slice.

## Summary

Adds:

- `durable_runtime_*` tables in the shared OpenClaw state DB;
- SQLite store lifecycle with schema version checks and shared state permission hardening;
- runtime runs, steps, events, refs, links, timers, and signals;
- local-first claim/release, heartbeat, recovery, and bounded worker helpers;
- read-only CLI and Gateway inspection surfaces;
- generic coordination projection with unsupported write controls disabled;
- Kysely generated types and guardrails for the new schema;
- public CLI docs for enablement, env vars, storage, and input retention.

## Explicit Non-Scope

- Work module behavior.
- Workboard UI/tools.
- Task Flow projection adapters.
- Retention/compaction policy.
- Postgres/multi-worker lease contention.
- Automatic retry/resume policy.
- Ledger-only write controls.

## Latest Reviewer Follow-Up

Updated on 2026-07-02 after rebasing onto upstream `origin/main` commit `133ce01e4a`.

Head: `3e39e28135d81586a2851bc68f5d554527ac70d0`.

Addressed ClawSweeper P1 findings:

- Future durable schema detection now runs immediately after `durable_schema_migrations` is available and before any `durable_runtime_*` table DDL, ALTER, or backfill work.
- The branch was rebased onto current upstream main; GitHub now reports the PR as conflict-free.

Regression coverage added:

- `src/durable/recovery.test.ts` advances fake timers with durable runtime enabled and no worker flag, then asserts no shared SQLite state file is created.
- `src/durable/sqlite-store.test.ts` opens a DB stamped with a newer durable schema version, expects rejection, and verifies no `durable_runtime_*` tables were created before the throw.

## Evidence

target.title: feat(slack): add ignoreOtherMentions channel config
target.body:
## Summary

- Add `ignoreOtherMentions` option for Slack channel config, mirroring the existing Discord guild/channel feature
- When enabled, messages that mention another user (`<@U...>`) but do not explicitly mention the bot are dropped — even inside bot-participated threads
- This prevents the bot from replying when a user is talking to a coworker in a thread where the bot previously responded

## Slack vs Discord difference

Discord's `ignoreOtherMentions` checks `!wasMentioned && !implicitMention`. The Slack version intentionally omits the `!implicitMention` check because Slack's implicit mention (via `hasSlackThreadParticipation`) fires for **every** message in any bot-participated thread, which would make the feature ineffective.

## Config example

```json5
{
  channels: {
    slack: {
      channels: {
        "*": { ignoreOtherMentions: true },
      },
    },
  },
}
```

| `src/config/types.slack.ts` | Add `ignoreOtherMentions` to `SlackChannelConfig` |

target.title: feat: add tools.fs.roots — per-agent filesystem roots with access modes
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: `tools.fs.workspaceOnly` is binary, so operators cannot safely allow agents to read or write a specific host path outside the workspace without opening broader filesystem access.
- Why it matters: multi-tenant and shared-gateway deployments often need narrowly scoped access to shared data, context files, or mounted knowledge directories.
- What changed: added `tools.fs.roots`, an explicit allowlist of filesystem roots with per-root `kind` (`dir`/`file`) and `access` (`ro`/`rw`), wired through host-mode FS tools, `apply_patch`, local media loading, outbound local-media/reply-delivery paths, and prompt-image auto-load.
- Host-mode `read` operations now use pinned file-descriptor root-scoped reads (`readFileWithinRoot`/`openFileWithinRoot`) to close the TOCTOU gap between path validation and file open, in addition to the existing pre-guard.
- Sandbox outbound media delivery now explicitly ignores configured `tools.fs.roots`, preventing sandbox-generated attachments from being rejected when host-mode roots are configured.
- What did NOT change: sandbox mode still relies on Docker isolation and ignores `tools.fs.roots`; `exec` sandboxing is unchanged; `tools.allow` / `tools.deny` behavior is unchanged.

## Change Type (select all)

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [x] Docs
- [x] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [x] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [x] Integrations
- [x] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #
- Related #
- [ ] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause / Regression History (if applicable)

- Root cause: existing FS policy exposed only two modes for host paths: workspace-only or unrestricted.
- Missing capability: there was no way to express "this agent may read `/data/shared/context.md` but may not read the rest of the host".
- Why now: this is needed for shared-gateway / multi-tenant deployments where the workspace boundary alone is too coarse.
- If unknown, what was ruled out: sandbox mode stays out of scope because sandbox tools resolve container paths, not host paths, and partial host-path enforcement there would create an inconsistent security model.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

- Coverage level that should catch this:
  - [x] Unit test
  - [x] Seam / integration test
  - [ ] End-to-end test
  - [ ] Existing coverage already sufficient
- Target tests/files:
  - `src/agents/tool-fs-policy.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/pi-tools.multi-root-guard.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/pi-tools.sandbox-mounted-paths.workspace-only.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/pi-tools.workspace-only-false.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/apply-patch.test.ts`
  - `src/media/local-roots.test.ts`
  - `src/media/load-options.test.ts`
  - `src/media/local-media-access.test.ts`
  - `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-media-paths.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/run/images.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/tools/image-tool.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/tools/image-generate-tool.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/tools/pdf-tool.test.ts`
  - `src/infra/outbound/deliver.test.ts`
  - `src/infra/fs-safe.test.ts`
  - `src/infra/fs-pinned-write-helper.spawn-error.test.ts`
  - `src/infra/fs-safe.unlink-helper-error.test.ts`
  - `extensions/googlechat/src/actions.test.ts`
  - `extensions/googlechat/src/channel.test.ts`
  - `extensions/feishu/src/media.test.ts`
  - `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/reply-delivery.test.ts`
- Scenarios locked in:
  - lexical dir/file root matching and ro/rw enforcement
  - canonical-root precedence over alias roots for host-mode mutation paths
  - unlink/delete behavior preserving symlink-entry semantics while still respecting stricter canonical roots
  - roots precedence over `workspaceOnly` for host-mode FS access
  - sandbox-mode fallback still honoring `workspaceOnly`
  - rooted local image/PDF/reference-image loads outside the workspace
  - rooted outbound local-media and reply-delivery paths preserving file-vs-dir root semantics
  - rooted prompt-image auto-load outside the workspace
  - host-mode reads use pinned-FD root-scoped operations (TOCTOU-safe)
  - sandboxed outbound media delivery ignores configured host roots
  - rooted delete helper gracefully falls back when pinned write helper spawn fails
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: the risky surfaces here are policy resolution, host-path mutation, and media path propagation, so targeted seam tests catch the actual failure modes without requiring a full live deployment.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

- New config surface: `tools.fs.roots` on global `tools.fs` and per-agent `tools.fs`.
- Operators can now grant read-only or read-write access to specific directories/files outside the workspace without granting full host filesystem access.
- Host-mode `read` / `write` / `edit` / `apply_patch` now respect those explicit roots.
- Local media loading, outbound local-media/reply-delivery flows, and prompt-image auto-load now preserve and enforce rooted file/dir access semantics.
- When both `roots` and `workspaceOnly` are set, `roots` takes precedence for host-mode FS access and a warning is logged.

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? (`Yes/No`) Yes
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- New/changed network calls? (`Yes/No`) No
- Command/tool execution surface changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- Data access scope changed? (`Yes/No`) Yes
- If any `Yes`, explain risk + mitigation:
  - This adds a new operator-controlled path restriction model for host-mode FS access. Risk is policy misunderstanding or incomplete enforcement across FS-adjacent surfaces. Mitigation: all configured roots are validated as absolute paths; enforcement is alias-safe; canonical root precedence is preserved for host-mode mutation paths; host-mode `read`/`write`/`edit`/`apply_patch`, local media inputs, outbound local-media/reply-delivery, and prompt-image auto-load are covered; host-mode reads use pinned-FD root-scoped operations to close TOCTOU gaps; sandbox mode explicitly ignores roots to avoid host/container path confusion.

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: macOS 15 / darwin 25.3.0
- Runtime/container: local repo checkout
- Model/provider: N/A for core FS policy; targeted local media tests use mocked image/PDF/image-generation providers
- Integration/channel (if any): host-mode FS tools + local media loading + outbound local-media reply flows
- Relevant config (redacted):

```json5
{
  "tools": {
    "fs": {
      "roots": [
        { "path": "/opt/app/workspaces/agent-1", "kind": "dir", "access": "rw" },
        { "path": "/data/finance/invoices", "kind": "dir", "access": "ro" },
        { "path": "/data/finance/context.md", "kind": "file", "access": "ro" }
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

### Steps

1. Configure an agent with `tools.fs.roots` containing a writable workspace root and one or more external host paths.
2. Attempt `read`/`write`/`edit`/`apply_patch` and local media access both inside and outside those roots.

target.title: fix(telegram): distinguish and render streamed reasoning/commentary progress lanes
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves Fixes an issue where Telegram users watching a streamed reply saw **no formatting at all** in the live progress draft: reasoning and commentary were indistinguishable (no lane markers, both plain), and the model's Markdown (`**`, backticks, `_…_`) either leaked as literal characters or was silently stripped. Three stacked defects, found by driving a live bot and inspecting the exact payloads: 1. **No lane identity.** The Telegram channel never passed the compositor's per-channel lane markers, so reasoning and commentary rendered identically (Discord passes 🧠/💬 and renders reasoning italic, commentary plain). 2. **Wrong renderer for lane text.** Progress lane bodies were hand-escaped rather than Markdown-rendered, so `**bold**`/backticks leaked raw; long reasoning lines additionally lost their closing `_` to truncation and degraded from italic to plain. 3. **`
` broke every multi-line preview at the transport.** Progress drafts join rendered lines with `
`, but Bot API `parse_mode=HTML` has no `
` tag — Telegram rejected every multi-line preview edit with "can't parse entities", and the parse-error fallback silently downgraded the whole draft to unformatted plain text. Because of this, streamed progress formatting effectively **never rendered** on non-rich Telegram accounts, whatever the payload said. ## Why This Change Was Made Three focused fixes, one per commit: 1. **Lane rendering** — pass the `🧠`/`💬` lane prefixes and `commentaryItalics: false` to the shared progress-draft compositor (mirroring the Discord channel), and render lane bodies through `renderTelegramHtmlText` (the `parse_mode=HTML`-safe converter). Lane lines collapse to one line first — multi-line commentary otherwise forms block markdown (a `\n\n---\n\n` separator turns the paragraph above it into a setext `

`, which Telegram rejects). Long lines clip *inside* the whole-line `_…_` wrapper so truncation can't chop the closing underscore. 2. **Transport** — convert `
` joins to literal newlines in the `parse_mode=HTML` transport branch, matching what the rich-message branch already does. 3. **Preview lifetime** — keep the streaming preview on screen ≥4s from first appearance before a teardown delete, scheduled detached (never awaited) so turn teardown is not stalled; on fast turns the box otherwise flashed away unread, and the immediate delete could race a just-persisted message. Non-goals: final-answer rendering and the durable (`/verbose on`) lanes are untouched — this is only the streamed progress window. ## User Impact Telegram users watching a streamed reply now see a formatted progress draft for the first time: reasoning (🧠, *italic*) clearly distinct from commentary (💬, plain), with the model's Markdown rendered — bold step names, monospace commands — instead of leaking or being stripped, and the progress box stays readable on fast turns. Biggest improvement for deepseek, which narrates progress almost entirely through its markdown-heavy reasoning lane. ## Evidence **Live capture** (dev gateway on this branch, Telegram Desktop, anthropic sonnet, `/reasoning stream`, fresh session). Same turn, in order: Reasoning lane — `🧠` + italic, with the model's `**bold**` rendered bold-italic and backtick commands in monospace, all inside the italic wrapper: ![reasoning zoom](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/proof-assets-telegram-progress-lanes/telegram-streamed-progress-lanes/pr-proof-2b-reasoning-zoom.png) Commentary lane — `💬` + upright, bold step names, monospace commands (contrast with the italic reasoning above): ![commentary zoom](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/proof-assets-telegram-progress-lanes/telegram-streamed-progress-lanes/pr-proof-3b-commentary-zoom.png) Full-stage frames: [prompt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/proof-assets-telegram-progress-lanes/telegram-streamed-progress-lanes/pr-proof-1-prompt.png) · [🧠 reasoning](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/proof-assets-telegram-progress-lanes/telegram-streamed-progress-lanes/pr-proof-2-reasoning-italic.png) · [💬 commentary](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/proof-assets-telegram-progress-lanes/telegram-streamed-progress-lanes/pr-proof-3-commentary.png) · [💬 step 3](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/proof-assets-telegram-progress-lanes/telegram-streamed-progress-lanes/pr-proof-4-commentary2.png) · [final](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/proof-assets-telegram-progress-lanes/telegram-streamed-progress-lanes/pr-proof-5-final.png) **Why the transport fix is required:** before it, the exact same preview payload was rejected by Telegram (`
` in `parse_mode=HTML`) and the live bubble showed the stripped plain fallback — verified by driving the intermediate build, which rendered everything plain despite a correct payload. **Before payload** (current `main`, same input, captured through the real dispatch): both lanes italic, no markers, raw markdown leaking — ```html Barnacling
Running `date`, then reading AGENTS.md
**Step 1: Running `date`.** ``` **Tests** — `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-dispatch.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/draft-stream.test.ts` → **198 passed**. New coverage: markdown rendering in both lanes, clipped-long-reasoning stays italic, multi-line commentary stays `parse_mode`-safe (the setext-`

` trap), `
`→newline transport conversion, and the ≥4s dwell timing.

target.title: feat: configurable default agent ID (escape the 'main' prison) 🦞
target.body:
## Summary

Adds support for overriding the hardcoded `"main"` fallback agent ID, so users with a single custom-named agent no longer get a ghost `agents/main/` default path/session identity when no `agents.list` is configured.

## The Problem

`DEFAULT_AGENT_ID` falls back to `"main"`. Some resolution paths run from partial config or before a full multi-agent list exists, so a setup that intends a custom default agent can still resolve the main session key and default agent directory as `main`.

## Solution

Two complementary override mechanisms:

### 1. Config key: `agents.defaultAgentId`

```json
{
  "agents": {
    "defaultAgentId": "maine-lobster"
  }
}
```

### 2. Env var: `OPENCLAW_DEFAULT_AGENT_ID`

```bash
export OPENCLAW_DEFAULT_AGENT_ID=maine-lobster
```

### Priority (highest → lowest)

1. `agents.list[].default: true` (explicit default agent)
2. `agents.list[0]` (first configured agent)
3. `agents.defaultAgentId` config key
4. `OPENCLAW_DEFAULT_AGENT_ID` env var
5. Hardcoded `"main"` (backward compatible)

## Changes

- Adds `agents.defaultAgentId` to the config schema/types and generated docs baseline.
- Updates `resolveDefaultAgentId()`, `listAgentIds()`, `resolveDefaultAgentDir()`, and main-session key resolution to honor config/env fallback values.
- Keeps populated `agents.list` behavior unchanged: list default/first entry still wins.
- Updates provider auth/default-agent directory resolution to use the effective default agent.
- Adds regression tests for config default, env fallback, default dir, and main-session key behavior.

## Testing

- `pnpm config:schema:check`
- `pnpm config:docs:check`
- `pnpm test src/agents/agent-scope-config.test.ts src/config/sessions/main-session.test.ts src/config/sessions/session-key.test.ts src/commands/auth-choice.test.ts src/commands/auth-choice.apply.plugin-provider.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`
- `pnpm check:changed`
- `git merge-tree --write-tree HEAD origin/main` → merge-clean

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: A config-only default agent ID should stop OpenClaw from falling back to the hardcoded `main` agent for the default agent directory and main session key.
- **Real environment tested**: Local OpenClaw checkout rebased onto latest `origin/main`, running the patched TypeScript source directly with Node/tsx in `/root/.openclaw/workspace/openclaw-pr-acpx/pr-51762`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```console
$ node --import tsx --input-type=module <<'EOF'
import { resolveDefaultAgentId, resolveDefaultAgentDir } from './src/agents/agent-scope-config.ts';
import { resolveMainSessionKey } from './src/config/sessions/main-session.ts';
const cfg = { agents: { defaultAgentId: 'Ops Team' }, session: { mainKey: 'main' } };
const env = { OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR: '/tmp/openclaw-real-proof' };
console.log('defaultAgentId=' + resolveDefaultAgentId(cfg, env));
console.log('defaultAgentDir=' + resolveDefaultAgentDir(cfg, env));
console.log('mainSessionKey=' + resolveMainSessionKey(cfg, env));
EOF
```

- **Evidence after fix**: Terminal output copied from the patched real source command above:

```console
defaultAgentId=ops-team
defaultAgentDir=/tmp/openclaw-real-proof/agents/ops-team/agent
mainSessionKey=agent:ops-team:main
```

- **Observed result after fix**: `agents.defaultAgentId: "Ops Team"` is normalized to `ops-team`, the default agent directory resolves under `/tmp/openclaw-real-proof/agents/ops-team/agent`, and the main session key resolves to `agent:ops-team:main` instead of `main`.
- **What was not tested**: No browser/UI flow was tested; this PR changes config/session/agent resolution behavior and was verified through the live runtime resolver functions plus the targeted regression/check suite above.
